opener: Father, I keep looking at what's written on the paper — the promise, the prophecy, the thing You already said was mine — and I still haven't walked into it.
paragraphs: I'm tired of standing at the edge of my own inheritance like a tourist with a brochure. I can quote the promise. I can recite the verse. But I haven't moved my furniture in — I haven't stopped sleeping in the old defeat like it's still my address, even though You signed the deed a long time ago. There's a version of my life I keep visiting on good days and leaving before dark, and I'm done living like a guest in what You called mine.

So burn off what's been sitting on the land that isn't supposed to be there anymore — the shame I keep farming instead of the harvest, the fear I water better than my faith, the old name I answer to faster than the new one You gave me. Give me the courage to possess what You already settled, not just admire it from the road. I stop waiting for permission I was given before I was born. In Jesus' name, amen.
bold: I stop waiting for permission I was given before I was born
kicker: A Prayer For What You Keep Visiting Instead Of Living In
footerNote: Save this for the promise you've been standing outside of
